text: If you could have dinner tonight with anyone at all, who would you pick and what would you want to talk about?
why: Reveals whom she admires and what she wants from them; the natural follow-up is what first drew her to that person.

text: What would a perfect day look like for you, from waking up to going to bed?
why: Reveals how she wants to spend time and who is in the day; the follow-up is which part of it she already has.

text: If you woke up tomorrow with one new ability or quality, what would you want it to be, and what would change first?
why: Reveals the gap she feels in herself; the follow-up is what she would do first with it.

text: If you could live to ninety and keep either the mind or the body of a thirty-year-old for the last sixty years, which would you keep?
why: Reveals which part of herself she counts as herself; the follow-up is what she imagines losing with the other.

text: When did you last sing to yourself, and what was it?
why: Reveals a private, unguarded habit; the follow-up is what puts her in that mood.

text: What is something small you do most days purely because you like it?
why: Reveals what she protects in an ordinary day; the follow-up is how long it has been in her routine.

text: What do you find yourself reading about or watching when nobody has asked you to?
why: Reveals unpaid curiosity rather than credentials; the follow-up is where the interest started.

text: What time of day do you feel most like yourself, and what are you usually doing then?
why: Reveals the conditions under which she feels most herself; the follow-up is what the rest of the day costs her.

text: What is something in your home that nobody else would notice, but that you would notice if it were gone?
why: Reveals a private attachment to an ordinary object; the follow-up is how it got there.

text: What song or smell drops you straight back into a particular time in your life?
why: Reveals a period that still has a hold on her; the follow-up is what that time was like.

text: What have you been enjoying lately that you did not expect to enjoy?
why: Reveals a taste in motion and her willingness to be surprised; the follow-up is what she expected instead.

text: What is something you like doing enough that you are happy to keep doing it badly?
why: Reveals where she is free of wanting to be good at something; the follow-up is how bad she actually is.

text: Which place you have spent time in do you miss, and what is it you miss about it?
why: Reveals what a place gives her that she is without now; the follow-up is whether she would go back.

text: What is a small moment from the last year or so that you still think about?
why: Reveals what registers with her at ordinary scale; the follow-up is why that one stuck.

text: What is something a friend of yours does that you have quietly started copying?
why: Reveals what she admires closely enough to take on; the follow-up is what that friend is like.

text: If a crystal ball could tell you one true thing about yourself, your life or your future, what would you ask it?
why: Reveals the open question she is carrying; the follow-up is whether she would actually want the answer.

text: If your home caught fire and everyone in it was already safe, what one object would you go back for?
why: Reveals which object carries meaning rather than value; the follow-up is the story attached to it.

text: If you were handed a year with no obligations in it, what would you actually do with it?
why: Reveals what she wants when nothing is required of her; the follow-up is what makes it impossible now.

text: If you could make one person understand exactly how you feel about them without having to explain it, who would you pick, and what would they finally understand?
why: Reveals an unsaid feeling and who it is aimed at; the follow-up is why it has stayed unsaid.

text: If you could arrange for someone you love to get something they want but would never ask for, what would you arrange?
why: Reveals how closely she reads the people around her; the follow-up is how she knows they want it.

text: What is something you have wanted to do for a long time and not done, and what has stopped you?
why: Reveals a live want and the obstacle she names for it; the follow-up is what would have to change.

text: What are you most grateful for in your life as it is now?
why: Reveals what she counts as good fortune; the follow-up is how it came about.

text: What is your most treasured memory?
why: Reveals a scene she has chosen to keep; the follow-up is who else was there.

text: What is something you have changed your mind about, where you can still remember what changed it?
why: Reveals how she updates and what moves her; the follow-up is what she thought before.

text: How do you usually show someone you care about them when you are not saying it out loud?
why: Reveals her actual affectionate behaviour rather than a label for it; the follow-up is whether people notice.

text: What is a running joke between you and someone in your life that you would struggle to explain to anyone else?
why: Reveals a close relationship through the humour inside it; the follow-up is how the joke started.

text: What do you value most in a friendship, and which friend do you think of when you say it?
why: Reveals the standard she holds people to; the follow-up is a friendship that has it.

text: What is a rule you have made for yourself that you actually keep?
why: Reveals a value she has turned into behaviour; the follow-up is what made her make the rule.

text: When you have a choice between doing something well and doing something new, which way do you lean?
why: Reveals what she optimises for when the two pull apart; the follow-up is a time she went the other way.

text: What do you think deserves more attention than it gets?
why: Reveals what she thinks is undervalued and why; the follow-up is how she came to notice it.

text: What makes somewhere feel like home to you?
why: Reveals the conditions she needs to settle; the follow-up is where she has had them.

text: If you knew you had a year left and everything else carried on as normal, would you change how you are living, and what would you change?
why: Reveals the distance between how she lives and how she wants to; the follow-up is what is holding the current shape in place.

text: If you could set one condition that had to hold in every close relationship in your life, what would you set?
why: Reveals the non-negotiable she brings to closeness; the follow-up is what taught her to want it.

text: If you could pass one thing you believe on to someone you love and know they would take it on, what would you pass on?
why: Reveals a belief she holds strongly enough to want inherited; the follow-up is who she pictured.

text: If you had to keep the memories from one stretch of your life and let the rest blur, which stretch would you keep?
why: Reveals which period she counts as the important one; the follow-up is what was happening then.

text: If you had to hand someone one thing to watch or read so that they understood your sense of humour, what would you hand them?
why: Reveals her humour through a concrete choice; the follow-up is which part of it is most her.

text: What do you find easy to give the people close to you, whether that is time, attention or honesty, and what do you find harder?
why: Reveals both her strength and her limit in close relationships; the follow-up is what makes the harder one hard.

text: What is something about yourself you have come to accept rather than try to fix?
why: Reveals a settled self-assessment without asking for a flaw confession; the follow-up is when she stopped fighting it.

text: What part does laughing play in how you get through things?
why: Reveals humour as a working part of her life rather than a taste; the follow-up is who she laughs with.

text: What part do love and affection play in your life?
why: Reveals the weight she puts on being close to people; the follow-up is whether that has changed.

text: If we became close friends, what is the thing you would want me to know about you?
why: Reveals what she thinks is most necessary to understand her; the follow-up is what people usually miss.

text: What are three things you think we already have in common?
why: Reveals what she has noticed and chosen to name; the single 'we' item in the bank, kept as a closer at the end of a run.

text: What do you think people owe the people they are close to?
why: Reveals her sense of obligation inside relationships; the follow-up is where she thinks it ends.

text: What do you think is worth being fussy about, even when it annoys people?
why: Reveals a standard she will defend; the follow-up is the last time she insisted on it.

text: What do you think a good life has to have in it?
why: Reveals her working definition of a life worth having; the follow-up is which parts she already has.

text: What is the most embarrassing thing that has happened to you?
why: Reveals how she tells a story against herself; the follow-up is what she did next.

text: What is the most useless skill you have, and how did you end up with it?
why: Reveals an odd corner of her history; the follow-up is whether she can demonstrate it.

text: If you had to eat the same meal every day for a month, what would you pick, and how long before you cracked?
why: Reveals a plain taste and how seriously she takes food; the follow-up is where she eats it.

text: What were you intensely into as a kid that you would still defend now?
why: Reveals an early enthusiasm she has not disowned; the follow-up is what she saw in it.

text: If you had to give a ten-minute talk tomorrow with no preparation, what would you talk about?
why: Reveals what she carries ready-made in her head; the follow-up is how she knows so much about it.

text: What is the last thing you did purely because it seemed funny at the time?
why: Reveals her appetite for a silly idea; the follow-up is whether it was worth it.

text: If someone filmed an ordinary week of your life, what would the best scene be?
why: Reveals what she likes about her ordinary days; the follow-up is who else is in the scene.

text: What are you unreasonably competitive about?
why: Reveals where her pride sits, at a safe scale; the follow-up is her record at it.
